gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the four "built-in memory" cams use the term for two different setups. On the 70mai M500, the eMMC is the only storage and holds the loop recordings. On DDPAI's Z90 line, the 64GB eMMC works together with a microSD card of up to 512GB under DDPAI's D²save "Dual-Storage System". I could not open a page showing which footage stays on the eMMC once a card is inserted.
standout_why: I checked the pages ChatGPT cited. The DDPAI Z90 Master page (rank 6) is summed up in ChatGPT's answer as 'Built-in memory plus optional microSD expansion'. The 70mai M500 store page (rank 9) and InCarTec's M500 and 70mai listings (ranks 3 and 13) say 'Built-in eMMC'. The REDTIGER F77 page (rank 15) and the M800 manual (rank 16) are the others. Together they already cover that the DDPAI has eMMC plus microSD and the 70mai/REDTIGER have eMMC only. None of them gives eMMC hours per capacity or eMMC endurance, or shows on a page I opened which footage lands on the eMMC when a card is fitted. The useful version of this finding would be loop hours per GB at each model's top resolution, or 'the eMMC only keeps event clips once a card is in'. I could not source either one, so what I can add is only part of a finding. Most maker pages returned HTTP 429, and device.report, manuals.plus and pbtech returned 403.
decides: This mostly confirms the pick and changes price more than ranking. Dealectric already lists the DDPAI Z90 Pro, which DDPAI's US store sells for $199 today. It is a three-camera model (front 4K, rear 2K, interior 3K) with the same '64GB eMMC + 512GB microSD' D²save storage. That is $100 under the Z90 Master ChatGPT showed ($299). A shopper who strictly wants no card at all is better matched by the 70mai M500 (eMMC only). The page should say in plain words that the DDPAI eMMC sits alongside a card and does not replace it.
